title: The Loyalty Tax
hook: Stop being a "loyal" employee. You’re actually paying a tax.
script:
(Visual: Split screen. Left side: Person staying at one company for 5 years. Right side: Person switching every 2 years.)

"Most Indian professionals treat their job like a marriage. They value loyalty. But in a corporate structure, loyalty is a liability."

(Cut to: Text overlay 'The Loyalty Tax')

"Here is the math: Annual increments usually hover around 5-10%. But a strategic jump usually nets 30% to 100%. 

When you stay, you aren't being loyal to the company; you are subsidizing their payroll. You are paying a 'Loyalty Tax'—the difference between your current salary and your actual market value."

(Cut to: Close up)

"The company isn't rewarding your stability; they are rewarding your willingness to be underpaid. Your value isn't decided by your boss; it's decided by the market. Stop asking for a raise. Start asking for a new offer."
caption: Loyalty is a virtue in friendships, but a financial mistake in careers. If your salary growth is slower than the market rate, you aren't being loyal—you're being expensive to yourself. 📉 #RationalThoughts #CareerStrategy #CorporateIndia #FirstPrinciples
